title: terraform destroy takes out production and its backups
summary: The founder of DataTalks.Club was moving a site to AWS and reused the Terraform setup of his production platform. Claude Code restored an older state file that described production and then ran a destroy. The network, the cluster, the load balancers and the database went, along with the snapshots he had counted on as backups: two and a half years of course data. By his own account he saw the command and did not stop it.
lesson: A prompt you can approve in a hurry is not enough for commands like this. Make destroy impossible for the agent and run it yourself.

sources.title: Alexey Grigorev: How I dropped our production database
Tom's Hardware: Claude Code deletes a production setup, database and snapshots

scenarios.note: With Terraform's own confirmation switched off.
